newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan peace factions choose united leader.
newsitem.headline: Sudan peace factions choose united leader.

text.p: Sudanese factions which signed a peace treaty with the Khartoum government last week have chosen Riek Machar as their leader, the official Sudanese news agency SUNA said on Tuesday.
Machar is head of the South Sudan Independence Movement, the largest of five groups which made a deal with the Khartoum government.
Khartoum sees the accord as the best hope for ending the war in which the largely Christian and animist south is fighting what it sees as domination by the Moslem and Arab north.
The peace agreement calls for a referendum among southern Sudanese after an interim period of four years to find out whether they want to secede or remain part of Sudan.
The Sudan People's Liberation Army, the group with the largest military force, rejected the peace agreement saying it wanted to overthrow the Islamist government in Khartoum.
It is fighting in alliance with northern opposition forces under the umbrella of the National Democratic Alliance.
The five factions are united in the agreement under the name United Democratic Salvation Front for Southern Sudan. SUNA said their united troops would be named South Sudan Defence Force.

Their new leader Machar, 44, holds a doctorate from a British university and is an engineer by profession. He is a former lecturer at the University of Khartoum, Sudan's most prestigious institution of higher learning.
He belongs to the Nuer tribe, the second largest tribe in southern sudan.
